bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42485275 (hoextdown): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target hoedown_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42485275
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source / staged poc
bug_description.normalized:
The staged 77-byte witness is exactly three lines: `[^  ]
`, `[^  ]:	` followed by 57 spaces and `
`, and ` :    ` with no final newline. In `hoedown_document_render()`, `is_footnote()` parses the second line as a footnote definition named two spaces and copies its body into a 64-byte heap buffer containing `	` + 57 spaces + `
:    `. During second-pass inline parsing of the first line, `char_link()` resolves the matching `[^  ]` footnote reference and moves the same `footnote_ref` into `doc->footnotes_used`, so `parse_footnote_list()` reparses that 64-byte buffer as footnote content. `parse_block()` recognizes the buffer as a definition list because the first line is term text and the second line begins with `:`, and `parse_definition()` passes the definition-body line `:    ` to `parse_listitem()`. There, `prefix_dt()` strips the `: ` marker, leaving exactly three spaces, and because fenced-code parsing is enabled `parse_listitem()` calls `is_codefence()` on that 3-byte slice. `is_codefence()` skips all three spaces so `i == size == 3`, then executes `c = data[i]` before checking `i + 2 >= size`. That late guard order reads one byte past the end of the 64-byte footnote-contents allocation and produces the saved `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1`. The fix adds the `i + 2 >= size` return before `c = data[i]`.

source.description: First project statement that copies attacker-controlled bytes into the heap buffer later reparsed and over-read by `is_codefence()`.
source.value_from: `gt_results/arvo_42485275/poc` is exactly `[^  ]\n[^  ]:\t` + 57 spaces + `\n :    `. This first `hoedown_buffer_put()` copies the second input line's post-colon payload, `\t` plus 57 spaces, into the new footnote `contents` buffer.
source.note: This is the earliest project-code materialization of the buffer that later becomes `ref->contents` and reaches the crash.

sink.description: Crash site. After `is_codefence()` consumes all three bytes of the short slice as optional spaces, this dereference reads one byte past the 64-byte footnote contents buffer.
sink.note: The saved ASan report is `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `is_codefence /src/hoextdown/src/document.c:1792:6`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `is_codefence()` performs `c = data[i]` before enforcing the size predicate `i + 2 >= size`; when the optional-space scan has already advanced `i` to `size`, the bounds check comes too late to protect the read.
root_cause.note: The patch moves `if (i + 2 >= size) return 0;` ahead of `c = data[i];`, which is exactly the missing pre-read obligation on this path.

parser_admitted.description: The testcase has already entered hoextdown's Markdown parser with footnotes, fenced code, and definition lists enabled, and the first pass is scanning the input lines for footnote definitions.

coarse_trace.summary: The first pass recognizes the second witness line as a footnote definition, copies its body into a 64-byte `contents` buffer, and registers that buffer in `doc->footnotes_found` under the footnote name consisting of two spaces.

Second-pass inline parsing of the first line `[^  ]` resolves the same footnote and moves its `footnote_ref` into `doc->footnotes_used`, after which `parse_footnote_list()` reparses the stored 64-byte `ref->contents` buffer.
The footnote body is recognized as a definition list because its second line begins with `:`, and the definition parser isolates the 5-byte body line `:    ` for list-item parsing.
Definition-list parsing strips the `: ` marker, leaving a 3-byte slice of only spaces, and because fenced-code parsing is enabled that short slice is tested with `is_codefence()`.
`is_codefence()` consumes all three bytes as optional leading spaces and then reads `data[i]` before its `i + 2 >= size` guard, causing the saved 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.code: hoedown_buffer_put(contents, data + start + ind, i - start - ind);
fine_trace.note: Source. While parsing the footnote definition line `[^  ]:\t` + 57 spaces, `is_footnote()` copies the post-colon payload into `contents`. For this witness the first copied chunk is exactly `\t` plus 57 spaces, so `contents->size` becomes 58.
Because the first content line ended with a newline in the input, the parser appends `\n` to the same heap buffer. The buffered footnote body is now 59 bytes long.

fine_trace.code: hoedown_buffer_put(contents, data + start + ind, i - start - ind);
fine_trace.note: On the third witness line ` :    `, `is_footnote()` strips the single leading space (`ind == 1`) and appends only `:    ` (5 bytes). The resulting footnote-body buffer is exactly 64 bytes long: `\t` + 57 spaces + `\n:    `, matching the ASan allocation region `[0x606000000440,0x606000000480)`.

The parsed footnote definition is registered in `doc->footnotes_found` under the name consisting of two spaces. The same `footnote_ref` now aliases the 64-byte `contents` buffer through `ref->contents`.

During second-pass inline parsing of the remaining first line `[^  ]`, `char_link()` materializes the same two-space footnote id, finds the `footnote_ref` created in step 4, and appends that same object to `doc->footnotes_used`. This is the alias that makes the stored 64-byte body reachable by `parse_footnote_list()`.

fine_trace.code: parse_footnote_def(work, doc, ref->num, ref->name, ref->contents->data, ref->contents->size);
fine_trace.note: When hoextdown renders used footnotes, it reparses the exact same buffer from step 4. The footnote body re-entering the block parser is still the 64-byte sequence `\t` + 57 spaces + `\n:    `.

fine_trace.code:
else if ((doc->ext_flags & HOEDOWN_EXT_DEFINITION_LISTS) && prefix_dli(doc, txt_data, end))
	beg += parse_list(ob, doc, txt_data, end, HOEDOWN_LIST_DEFINITION);
fine_trace.note: On this footnote body, `prefix_dli()` treats the first line (`\t` plus spaces) as definition-term text and the second line `:    ` as a definition entry, so the body is dispatched into the definition-list parser. For this witness, the definition-body offset is 59 bytes into `ref->contents`.

fine_trace.code: j = parse_listitem(ob, doc, data + end, size - end, flags, attribute);
fine_trace.note: After the definition-term scan, `parse_definition()` passes only the definition-body line to `parse_listitem()`. Here `end == 59`, so the slice is exactly the trailing 5-byte string `:    ` from the 64-byte footnote buffer.

Because this is a definition-list item, `prefix_dt(":    ", 5)` returns 2 and strips the `: ` marker. `parse_listitem()` therefore calls `is_codefence()` on `data + beg`, which is the last 3 bytes of the footnote buffer: three spaces at offsets 61, 62, and 63 of the 64-byte allocation.

The fence probe receives a 3-byte slice of only spaces. The nested optional-space checks consume every byte, so `i` advances from 0 to 3 and now equals `size` before the function looks for a fence character.

Root cause and sink. With `i == size == 3`, the probe slice already points at `ref->contents->data + 61`, so `c = data[i]` dereferences offset 64 of the 64-byte footnote allocation. The only size guard, `i + 2 >= size`, is evaluated too late because the out-of-bounds byte has already been read. This is the saved `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `is_codefence`.

allocation_context.description: ASan's allocation stack reaches `hoedown_buffer_put()` from this `is_footnote()` call site when the copied footnote body grows to the 64-byte buffer later passed into `is_codefence()`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The ASan allocation stack points to `is_footnote()` growing the 64-byte footnote `contents` buffer, and the fine trace follows that same buffer through `ref->contents`, `doc->footnotes_used`, and the 3-byte `is_codefence()` slice to the out-of-bounds read.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: The copied footnote body from steps 1-3 is stored in `ref->contents`, reparsed through `parse_footnote_list()` and `parse_definition()`, reduced to a 3-byte all-space slice by `parse_listitem()`, and then read out of bounds by `is_codefence()` at step 11.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42485275 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `hoedown_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `is_codefence` with stack `parse_listitem -> parse_definition -> parse_list -> parse_block -> parse_footnote_def -> parse_footnote_list`.

format.name: 3-line Markdown footnote-definition witness
format.contract:
The witnessed trigger is exactly the staged 77-byte input: line 1 `[^  ]
`; line 2 `[^  ]:	` followed by 57 ASCII spaces and `
`; line 3 ` :    ` with no trailing newline. With the hoedown fuzzer's enabled extensions, that exact structure registers a footnote named two spaces, leaves a matching `[^  ]` footnote reference in the remaining document text so the footnote is marked used, builds a 64-byte footnote body `	` + 57 spaces + `
:    `, and strips the final `: ` so `is_codefence()` is invoked on exactly three spaces.
